newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH VAN LANSCHOT SEES 96 NET UP AT LEAST 20 PCT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH VAN LANSCHOT SEES 96 NET UP AT LEAST 20 PCT.

text.p: Dutch Bank F. van Lanschot Bankiers said on Monday it expects net profits to rise at least 20 percent in full-year 1996.
"This is an indicative figure," the bank's chief executive officer Bert Heemskerk told a press lunch.
In 1995, the bank posted a net profit of 56 million guilders, a 27.5 percent rise year on year.
In September 1996, the bank reported a 31 percent increase in net profit to 31.5 million guilders over the first half year.
Heemskerk said a rise in the number of private clients both at home and abroad, combined with an increase in small-company clients and more private loans business had boosted revenues.
Heemskerk said he saw good prospects for 1997 as well, as the market segments in which the bank is active continued to grow.

"The market for wealthy private investors and small-company clients continues to grow, while there are still unexploited opportunities as regards institutional investors and corporates," Heemskerk said.
Investor interest in the bank's new stock index-linked investment funds also continued to grow, he added.
He said macro-economic factors also remained favourable to the bank's business.
Heemskerk repeated the bank intended to float part of its shares on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in 1998.
"Last April, we said we were planning to float 20 to 25 percent of our shares within the next two years, and that still stands. We're working on it," Heemskerk said.
